applies_when: learner encounters a surd with a fraction inside or in front

dbe_source.recommendation: Candidates struggled with two surds that had fractions. Handle the fraction inside the surd first, then isolate, then square.

lesson.concept: When the surd contains a fraction, isolate the surd first, then square. One step at a time.
lesson.why: Fractional surds are the hardest shape in the section. The examiner looks for the isolation line and the squaring line as separate marks.

work: Let k = 1/sqrt(x). Then the equation reads sqrt(k + 2) = k.

probe.hint: Square both sides, solve the quadratic in k, then reject the negative root.

learner_message: With a fractional surd, isolate first, then square. One step at a time.
